He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green Falcons]] where he was named to multiple All-[[Mid-American Conference]] teams.{{cite web |title=Richaun Holmes |url=https://bgsufalcons.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/richaun-holmes/5020 |access-date=July 24, 2023 |work=BGSUFalcons.com}}{{cite web|title=2015 DraftExpress NBA Mock Draft|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/nba-mock-draft/2015/|work=DraftExpress.com|access-date=April 26, 2015}}{{cite web|title=Richaun Holmes Player Profile|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/player/Richaun-Holmes/Summary/42932|work=RealGM.com|access-date=April 26, 2015}} Holmes previously played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for three seasons before being traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the 2018 offseason. He played one season with the Suns before signing with the [[Sacramento Kings]] in the 2019 offseason. He has also played for the [[Dallas Mavericks]] and the [[Washington Wizards]]. ==High school and college career== Holmes is the son of two [[Doctor of Divinity|Doctors of Divinity]] who run a [[Chicago]]-area church.{{cite news|first=Chris|last=Dortch|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/features/chris_dortch/06/04/2015-draft-feauture-richaun-holmes/|title=Overlooked at every level, Bowling Green's Richaun Holmes can do it all|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=June 4, 2015|access-date=July 6, 2015}} In high school, Holmes grew from a 6' 2" guard into a 6' 9" forward, but did not receive any [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] college basketball scholarship offers until he had already committed to playing for [[Moraine Valley Community College]], located in [[Illinois]]. In his only season at Moraine Valley, Holmes averaged 19.3 points, 9.3 rebounds and 5.2 blocks per game. After earning [[junior college]] All-American honors, Holmes transferred to [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green]].{{cite news|first=Mike|last=Walsh|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/post-tribune/sports/ct-sta-southtown-athletes-st-0301-20150227-story.html|title=Lockport grad Richaun Holmes hits 1,000-point landmark for Bowling Green|work=Chicago Tribune|date=February 27, 2015|access-date=April 20, 2020}} In his sophomore season at Bowling Green, Holmes averaged 6.5 points, 5.0 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game. He doubled his scoring numbers while contributing 7.7 rebounds and 2.5 blocks per game as a junior. With the hiring of coach [[Chris Jans]], Holmes worked on improving every aspect of his game and adding a [[three-point shot]], sometimes taking 1,000 shots a day in practice. The result was averages of 14.7 points, 8.0 rebounds and 2.7 blocks per game as a senior and shooting percentages of 56.3% on field goals and 41.9% on three-pointers. In Holmes' senior year, Bowling Green improved to 21–12 from a 12-win season the year prior, while also reaching the [[CollegeInsider.com Tournament]]. ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2015–2018)=== On June 25, 2015, Holmes was selected with the 37th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web |date=June 25, 2015 |title=76ers take Duke's Okafor with 3rd pick in NBA draft |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2015/06/26/ap-bkn-draft-76ers |access-date=November 13, 2024 |website=si.com}} On July 31, 2015, he signed with the 76ers after averaging 10 points and five rebounds in three [[2015 NBA Summer League|summer league]] games for the team.{{cite web |date=July 31, 2015 |title=Sixers Sign Richaun Holmes |url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150731-holmes-signed |url-status=dead |access-date=July 31, 2015 |publisher=National Basketball Association |archive-date=August 3, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150803014017/http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150731-holmes-signed }} On November 9, 2015, he received his first career start, scoring a then-season-high 11 points in a loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web |last=Gelston |first=Dan |date=November 9, 2015 |title=Bulls pull away in 2nd half, top winless 76ers 111–88 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151109/CHIPHI/gameinfo.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160112033613/http://www.nba.com/games/20151109/CHIPHI/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 12, 2016 |access-date=November 10, 2015 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} He topped that mark on December 10, 2015, with 14 points against the [[San Antonio Spurs]]. On December 28, 2015, he set a new season high with 18 points in a 95–91 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web |title=Richaun Holmes 2015-16 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/holmeri01/gamelog/2016 |access-date=December 17, 2015 |work=Basketball-Reference.com}} [[File:Richaun Holmes.jpg|thumb|right|Holmes scoring in 2018]] In July 2016, Holmes re-joined the 76ers for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web |date=July 1, 2016 |title=Ben Simmons Headlines Sixers Summer League Roster |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/philadelphia/news/ben-simmons-headlines-sixers-summer-league-roster |access-date=July 24, 2023 |work=CBSLocal.com}} In January 2017, he was assigned three times to the [[Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web |title=2016-17 NBA Assignments |url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/ |archive-date=January 26, 2017 |access-date=January 13, 2017 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} He became a fixture in the Sixers' rotation in February 2017 following the [[Nerlens Noel]] trade, the prolonged injury to [[Joel Embiid]], and Holmes outplaying fellow 2015 Sixers pick [[Jahlil Okafor]].{{cite web |last=Cooney |first=Bob |date=March 5, 2017 |title=Sixers' Richaun Holmes has become center of attention |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/sixers/20170306_Cooney__Sixers__Richaun_Holmes_has_become_center_of_attention.html |access-date=March 6, 2017 |work=Philadelphia Daily News}} On February 24, 2017, he had 12 points, 10 rebounds and five blocks to help the depleted 76ers defeat the [[Washington Wizards]] 120–112.{{cite web |date=February 24, 2017 |title=Covington, Saric lead Sixers to 120–112 win over Wizards |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900262 |access-date=February 24, 2017 |publisher=ESPN}} On March 20, 2017, he tied a career high in points with 24 and established a career best in rebounds with 14 in a 112–109 overtime loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web |date=March 20, 2017 |title=Magic storm back to beat 76ers 112–109 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900440 |access-date=March 21, 2017 |publisher=ESPN}} Nine days later, he set a new career high with 25 points in a 99–92 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |date=March 29, 2017 |title=Howard has 22 points, 20 rebounds in Hawks' win over 76ers |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900506 |access-date=March 30, 2017 |publisher=ESPN}} On October 8, 2017, Holmes was ruled out for approximately three weeks after being diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in the radial bone of his left wrist.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/holmes-injury-update|title=Holmes Injury Update|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=October 8, 2017|access-date=October 8, 2017}} On June 13, 2018, the 76ers announced they had exercised the fourth-year option on their contract with Holmes.{{cite web |last=Smith |first=Jeff |date=June 13, 2018 |title=Sixers exercise contract options for T.J. McConnell, Richaun Holmes |url=https://sixerswire.usatoday.com/2018/06/13/76ers-contract-options-tj-mcconnell-richaun-holmes-nba-offseason-2018-news |access-date=July 24, 2023 |publisher=USA Today}} ===Phoenix Suns (2018–2019)=== On July 20, 2018, Holmes was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] in exchange for cash considerations.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-complete-trades-philadelphia-and-brooklyn|title=Suns Complete Trades with Philadelphia and Brooklyn|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 20, 2018|access-date=July 20, 2018}} On November 6, he had season highs of 13 points and 10 rebounds in a 104–82 loss to the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |date=November 6, 2018 |title=LeVert scores 26 to lift Nets past struggling Suns 104-82 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070832 |access-date=November 8, 2018 |publisher=ESPN}} Holmes later recorded a new season high of 19 points in a 123–119 overtime loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] on December 10.{{Cite web |date=December 11, 2018 |title=Clippers @ Suns |url=https://www.nba.com/game/lac-vs-phx-0021800399/box-score#box-score |access-date=November 13, 2024 |website=NBA.com}} Holmes also recorded a [[double-double]] of 12 points and a new season high of 11 rebounds on March 15, 2019, during only 16 minutes of play in a 108–102 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |date=March 16, 2019 |title=Suns' Richaun Holmes: Double-double in 16 minutes |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/suns-richaun-holmes-double-double-in-16-minutes/ |access-date=July 24, 2023 |website=cbssports.com}} ===Sacramento Kings (2019–2023)=== [[File:Richaun Holmes in 2019 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Holmes with Sacramento in 2019]] On July 16, 2019, Holmes signed a two-year contract, worth $10 million, with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web |last=Nicholson |first=Nikki |date=July 16, 2019 |title=Kings Sign Richaun Holmes |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-richaun-holmes |access-date=July 16, 2019 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On August 6, 2021, Holmes re-signed with the Kings on a four-year, $55 million contract.{{cite web|title=Kings Re-Sign Richaun Holmes|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-re-sign-richaun-holmes|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=August 6, 2021|access-date=August 6, 2021}}{{Cite web |title=Richaun Holmes Re-Signs with Kings with 4-Year, $55M Contract in Free Agency |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2945342-richaun-holmes-re-signs-with-kings-with-4-year-55m-contract-in-free-agency |access-date=March 18, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report}} On March 18, 2022, he was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to personal issues.{{Cite web |date=March 18, 2022 |title=Kings Update Regarding Richaun Holmes |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-update-regarding-richaun-holmes |access-date=March 19, 2022 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2023–2024)=== On July 6, 2023, Holmes, along with the draft rights to [[Olivier-Maxence Prosper]], was traded from the [[Sacramento Kings]] to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|title=Sacramento Kings Complete Trade With Dallas Mavericks|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-complete-trade-with-dallas-mavericks|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023|access-date=July 24, 2023}} ===Washington Wizards (2024–2025)=== On February 8, 2024, Holmes and a future first-round pick were traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in exchange for [[Daniel Gafford]].{{cite web|title=Wizards Acquire Holmes, 2024 First Round Pick|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/wizards-acquire-holmes-2024-first-round-pick|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} On June 29, he signed an extension with the Wizards.{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Richaun Holmes Declines Option, Signs Extension With Wizards|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/06/richaun-holmes-declines-option-re-signs-with-wizards.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=June 29, 2024|access-date=June 29, 2024}} On July 14, 2025, Holmes was waived by the Wizards.{{Cite web |last=Scotto |first=Mike |date=July 14, 2025 |title=Washington Wizards Waive Richaun Holmes |url=https://x.com/MikeAScotto/status/1944864891581686086?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Etweet}} === Panathinaikos (2025–2026) === On 9 August 2025, Holmes signed with Panathinaikos of the Greek Basketball League (GBL) and the EuroLeague after Panathinaikos failed to secure Lithuanian centre [[Jonas Valančiūnas]], who ultimately remained in the NBA.{{cite web |date=August 9, 2025 |title=Panathinaikos Sign Center Richaun Holmes |url=https://www.instagram.com/reel/DNIlXZcsSfS/?igsh=MTJ4ZmJudjF3c3FndQ== |access-date=11 November 2025}} His contract is a two‑year deal with a 1+1 structure, allowing the club and player to evaluate the partnership after the first season.{{cite web | last=Maher | first=Rory | title=Richaun Holmes Signs Two-Year Contract With Panathinaikos | website=Hoops Rumors | date=2025-08-09 | url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/08/richaun-holmes-signs-two-year-contract-with-panathinaikos.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com | access-date=2025-12-09}}{{AI-retrieved source|date=March 2026|checked=no}} Holmes is reported to be one of the highest‑paid players in Europe, earning approximately €2.7 million for the first year.{{cite web |title=Holmes corona la nueva superplantilla del Panathinaikos |url=https://as.com/baloncesto/euroliga/holmes-corona-la-nueva-superplantilla-del-panathinaikos-n/?utm_source=chatgpt.com |website=AS.com |access-date=11 November 2025}}{{AI-retrieved source|date=March 2026|checked=no}} He made his debut for the club in a friendly tournament Final (the annual Pavlos Giannakopoulos Tournament) vs the Adelaide 36ers, registering 14 points and 10 rebounds as Panathinaikos won 106‑89.{{cite web |title=Richaun Holmes stands out in Panathinaikos debut |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1871061/richaun-holmes-stands-out-in-panathinaikos-debut/ |website=EuroHoops |access-date=11 November 2025}} In his fourth EuroLeague game of the 2025‑26 season, he produced perhaps his best performance for the club: 24 points and 10 rebounds in a 91–85 win over [[ASVEL Basket]], shooting 11 of 12 from the field and grabbing seven offensive rebounds.{{cite web |title=Birthday boost: Richaun Holmes erupts for 24 points as Panathinaikos edges ASVEL |url=https://www.talkbasket.net/204274-birthday-boost-richaun-holmes-erupts-for-24-points-as-panathinaikos-edges-asvel |website=TalkBasket.net |access-date=11 November 2025}} After only a handful of games into the 2025‑26 campaign, on 29 October 2025 Holmes was forced off in a EuroLeague home win over [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.]] with a knee injury, later diagnosed as a partial tear of the medial collateral ligament (MCL) in his right knee which will sideline him for approximately one month.{{cite web |title=Panathinaikos News: Holmes to Miss One Month, But No Long‑Term Damage |url=https://www.greekcitytimes.com/2025/10/29/panathinaikos-holmes-to-miss-one-month-but-no-long-term-damage/ |website=GreekCityTimes |access-date=11 November 2025}} On March 24, 2026, the team announced the termination of his contract. He had recently gotten into a public argument with the head coach, [[Ergin Ataman]] following a game on March 15th where the coach publicly called Holmes out for his lack of effort.{{cite web |title=Richaun Holmes leaves Panathinaikos following contract termination |url=https://basketnews.com/news-243732-richaun-holmes-leaves-panathinaikos-following-contract-termination.html
